Md Hamidur Rahman, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 
Amit Das Gupta, DAG with Rokeya Akhter, AAG, Abantee Nurul, AAG and Anna Khanom (Koli), AAG—For the Respondents.
parties:
Ilias Hossain (Md) and others ----- Petitioners
VS
The Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel, J: On an application under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inclusion of the case property measuring an area of 39 decimals of land out of SA Plot No.1058 corresponding to RS Plot No.679 appertaining to SA Khatian No.147 and RS Khatian No.42 of Mouza Dakkingaon, Police Station Shabujbagh, Dhaka at serial No.7 in 'Ka' schedule of vested properties published in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 2-5-2012 (Annexure-'H' to the writ petition) should not be declared to be without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and why the respondents should not be directed to release the case property from "Ka" schedule of vested property in favour of the petitioners and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule as set out in the writ petition, in short, are that CS Khatian No.118 of Mouza-Dakkhingaon under Police Station-Sabek Keraniganj, thereafter Tejgaon and at present-Sabujbag within District-Dhaka was prepared and published in the names of Brindaban Koibartta and Tufani Koibartta, both sons of Guru Proshad. In that khatian, 104 decimals of land were recorded under CS Plot No.1058 wherein they were the owners in equal shares. The said Tufani Koibartta died leaving behind his only son Pagol Nath Das who obtained 52 decimals of land in CS Plot No.1058 appertaining to CS Khatian No.118 of the aforesaid Mouza by way of inheritance from his deceased father. Thereafter, Pagol Nath Das sold out the said 52 decimals of land in favour of Abdus Samad Ahmed, son of Moulavi Tasir Uddin Ahmed vide registered sale deed being No.5763, dated 22-5-1957. Accordingly, SA Khatian No.147 covering 52 decimals of land in SA Plot No.1058 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad. During RS survey, RS Khatian No.42 covering 48 decimals of land in RS Plot No.679 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad Ahmed. 

3. Thereafter, Abdus Samad Ahmed sold out the said 52 decimals of land in favour of Rai Raman Mitra vide registered sale deed being No.1897, dated 17-1-1978. Out of the said 52 decimals of land, Rai Raman Mitra sold out 13 decimals of land to the instant petitioner No.1, Md Ilias Hossain vide registered sale deed being No.42072, dated 1-12-1978, (Annexure-B(i) of the writ petition). The said Rai Raman Mitra also sold out 26 decimals of land in favour of Mosammat Jahanara Begum, mother of the petitioner Nos.2-5 vide registered sale deed being No.42148, dated 1-12-1978, (Annexure-B(ii) of the writ petition). Thereafter, the petitioner No.I mutated his name in respect of 13.82 decimals of land vide Mutation Case No.5070 P-1/05, dated 12-5-2005. The said Mosammat Jahanara Begum out of her 26 decimals of land, sold out 5.61 decimals of land in favour of the petitioner Nos.6- 7 vide registered sale deed being No.3741, dated 28-6-1995, then 4.49 decimals of land in favour of the petitioner Nos.8-9 vide registered sale deed being No.3742, dated 28-6-1995 and 4.95 decimals of land in favour of Noorjahan Begum, mother of the petitioner Nos.10-12 vide registered sale deed being No.6113, dated 20-6-1988, (Annexure-C,C(i) and C(ii) of the writ petition). Thereafter, during Mohanagar Jarip, Mohanagar Khatian covering the case land were prepared and published in the names of the petitioner No.1, mother of the petitioner Nos.2-5, petitioner Nos.6-7, petitioner Nos.8-9 and mother of the petitioner Nos.10-12 accordingly without any objection from any quarter. The petitioner No.1 sold out 5.85 decimals of land in favour of the petitioner Nos.13-14 vide registered sale deed being No.5320, dated 14-7-2008, (Annexure-E & E(i) of the writ petition) and accordingly, they have mutated the said land in their respective names. The petitioner Nos.2-5 obtained 7.26 decimals of land by way of inheritance from their deceased mother Jahanara Begum and they have mutated the said land in their names (Annexure-F of the writ petition). The petitioners are possessing their 39 decimals of land for a long time since their respective date of purchase by erecting residential houses on the land. They have paid up to date revenue rent as per the latest Mohanagar khatian. 

4. On the 1st week of January, 2016 the petitioner No.1 went to the office of the respondent No.4, Tohsilder, Shabujbagh Tohshil Office for payment of his revenue rent for the year of 1422 BS, but the respondent No.4 refused to accept the rent on the ground that the land has been included in the list of vested property as "Ka" schedule land. Thereafter, on scrutiny, the petitioners found that SA Plot No.1058 corresponding to RS Plot No.679 covering their land has been included in the list of vested property, published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 2-5-2012 (Annexure-H of the writ petition). The property of the petitioners was vested to the Government in connection with VP Case No.523 of 1979. The petitioners came to know about the VP list on the 1st week of the January, 2016 and in the meantime, statutory period of limitation to apply before the Arpito Sampatti Prottorpan Tribunal, which was 31-12-2013 as per section 10 of the "অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১" elapsed. Being aggrieved by the inclusion of the said land of the petitioners at serial No. 7 in the list of 'Ka' schedule vested property Gazette, published on 2-5-2012, the petitioners finding no other alternative efficacious remedy filed the instant writ petition before this Hon'ble Court and obtained the present Rule. 

5. The Rule being served upon all the respondents, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, respondent No.2, entered appearance and filed an affidavit-in-opposition. 

6. Mr Md Hamidur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners at the very outset by referring to all the annexures submits that the petitioners have the title and possession over the case property and they never left the country. Therefore, the inclusion of the case property in 'Ka' list of the " অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১” is completely without any legal basis. 

7. He further submits that on a perusal of the annexure-H, it is found that the owner of the property in question was Joy Durga Bewa and others, but on perusal of the documents annexed herewith, it is apparent that never the property was recorded in the name of Joy Durga Bewa or others at any point of time, rather, SA, RS and latest Mohanagar Khatian has been prepared in the name of the present petitioners and their vendor or predecessor Abdus Samad. Hence, inclusion of the property in the 'Ka' schedule is not in accordance with law. 

8. Referring to the supplementary affidavit dated 12-11-2019, Mr Rahman submits that from the materials on record, it appears that Abdus Samad Ahmed sold out the said 52 decimals of land in favour of one Rairaman Mitra vide sale deed being No.1 897, dated 17-1-1978 and subsequently the petitioners obtained 39 decimals of land out of the said 52 decimals by way of purchase. Therefore, it is evident that at the relevant time, the case land belonged to Abdus Samad Ahmed, who never left the then East Pakistan. On the other hand, the said Abdus Samad Ahmed, the SA and RS recorded owner of the case land, was a Muslim. In that view of the matter, there is no scope to include the case land as vested property, but the respondents have acted arbitrarily by including the land of the petitioners in the 'Ka' schedule of the vested property, which is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority.

9. He finally submits that after 1974, the inclusion of the petitioners property in the list of vested property is illegal and also violative of Article 42 of the Constitution of Peoples Republic of Bangladesh. The petitioners can come directly to the High Court Division for protection of their right to property guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution of Peoples Republic of Bangladesh. Therefore, the writ petition is maintainable. To fortify his submissions, he relied upon the following decisions, which are as follows:-

10. Manabendra Chakrabarty vs Govern¬ment of Bangladesh, reported in 3 SCOB (2015) HCD 52; Government of Bangladesh represented by Ministry of Works and another vs Syed Chand Sultana, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 24; Saju Hosein vs Bangladesh, reported in 58 DLR (AD)1 7 7; Sharif Ashraf Uzzaman vs Bangladesh, reported in 2017 (2) LNJ (HCD) 166 = 70 DLR 857, and the case of Md Abdul Hye vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in LG (HCD) 6 = 70 DLR 313.

11. Per Contra, Mr Amit Das Gupta, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka by filing an affidavit-in-¬opposition submits that the Authority rightly and lawfully included the case property in the vested property list, published by Gazette notification dated 2-5-2012. He submits that the petitioners were fully aware about the Gazette notification and without going to the proper forum, being the Arpito Shampotti Tribunal for releasing their property, they filed the instant writ petition. They have no scope to prefer this writ petition as per the existing law of the land. As such, the instant writ petition is not maintainable, since they have alternative remedy.

12. He submits that the list of returnable property was prepared in order to return the property enlisted as vested property to the original owners, according to the Act of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১. Accordingly, on 2-5-2012, the Gazette was published following all the legal formalities.

13. He next submits that the mutation does not establish any right and title over any property, rather, mutation is normally allowed to realize Government Revenue. At the time of mutation of RS Khatian, the vested property Gazette notification was not published, as a result mutation Khatian was prepared in absence of the related vested property list. The property has been declared as vested property and leased out vide VP Case No.523 of 1979 and therefore, the purchase of the vested property by the petitioners is not proper as per law.

14. He finally submits that inclusion of the property in the 'Ka' schedule list of the vested property has been made following all the legal formalities, and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

15. We have considered the submissions made by the learned Advocate of the petitioners and the learned Deputy Attorney-General for the respondent No.2 and perused the writ petition, supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioners, affidavit-in-opposition and relevant annexures annexed thereto with profound attention.

16. It appears that the main cause to file this writ petition is the Gazette notification dated 2-5- 2012 (Annexure-H) wherein the petitioners property was included at serial No.7 as vested property. It appears from the record that the property in question that is CS Khatian No.118 of Mouza-Dakkhingaon under Police Station-Sabek Keraniganj, thereafter Tejgaon, at present¬Sabujbag within District-Dhaka was prepared and published in the names of Brindaban Koibartta and Tufani Koibartta, both sons of Guru Proshad. In that khatian, 104 decimals of land were recorded under CS Plot No.1058, as evidenced from the annexure-X of the writ petition. Thereafter, Tufani Koibartta died leaving behind his only son Pagol Nath Das who obtained 52 decimals of land in the CS Khatian No.118 of the aforesaid Mouza by way of inheritance from his deceased father and the said Pagol Nath Das sold out the said 52 decimals of land in favour of Abdus Samad Ahmed vide registered sale deed being No.5763, dated. 22-5-1957 (Annexure-Y of the writ petition). It appears that before SA survey, the said Abdus Samad Ahmed purchased 52 decimals of land and accordingly, SA Khatian No.147 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad Ahmed. Thereafter, during RS survey, RS Khatian No.42 was prepared and published in the name of said Abdus Samad Ahmed and 48 decimals of land was recorded in RS Plot No.679 of the said Khatian. Thereafter, Abdus Samad Ahmed sold out 52 decimals of land in favour of one Rai Raman Mitra vide registered sale deed No.1897, dated 17-1-1978. Subsequently, the present petitioners obtained 39 decimals of land out of said 52 decimals of land by way of purchase. It is clear from the record that at the relevant time of inclusion of the case land as vested property, the case land actually belonged to Abdus Samad Ahmed and hence the question of his whereabouts being unknown did not arise at all. Therefore, there is no basis to treat the case land as vested property.

17. From the above facts and upon perusal of the documents, it is clear that the petitioners name have been recorded in the record of right and they had paid rent. Moreover, there is nothing on record to indicate that they left the country. Rather, they have been possessing and enjoying the property since long by dint of their respective purchases.

18. Now, in respect to the issue of maintain¬ability of the present writ petition, it appears from the record that the Government has accepted rent from the petitioners up to 1421 BS and since their respective date of purchase, the petitioners are possessing the land by erecting residential houses on payment of revenue rent as per the latest Mohanagar Khatian as evidenced from annexures G to G (iv) respectively of the writ petition. Moreover, the possession of the petitioners has not been disturbed from any quarter in any way. Therefore, it is natural that they had no knowledge about their land being enlisted as vested property until the office of the respondent No.4 refused to accept the rent for the year of 1422 BS. Admittedly, by this time, the last date for filing a suit before the "অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যার্পণ আইন, ২০০১” expired. As such, they have no other alternative remedy other than filing this writ petition.

19. Further, as the petitioners have alleged of violation of their fundamental right, namely the right to property under Article 42 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, the present writ petition is very much maintainable. For invoking writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution, the petitioners do not require to show alternative, efficacious remedy. In this connection, reliance may be placed on the view of our Apex Court in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Syed Chand Sultana, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 24, wherein it has been held that:—
"The writ-petitioners can come directly to the High Court Division for protection of their fundamental right even though an alternative remedy is available." 

20. In the present case, it appears that the petitioners are in possession and continuously enjoying the case property since long on the basis of their purchase without any interruption of any quarter and they never left the country nor they have been dispossessed from the property in question. In such a situation, inclusion of their property in the "Ka" list of the vested property and treating it as vested property is violative of fundamental right to hold property as guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

21. It further appears that the Vested Property Case No.523 was started in the year of 1979. It has already been settled by our Apex Court in the case of Saju Hosein vs Bangladesh, reported in 58 DLR (AD) 177, that:—
"Since the law of enemy property itself died with the repeal of Ordinance No.1 of 1969 on 23-3-1974 no further vested property case can be started thereafter on the basis of the law which is already dead. Accordingly, there is no basis at all to treat the case land as vested property upon starting VP Case No.210 of 1980." 

22. Therefore, after 23-3-1974, there is no basis at all to start the Vested Property Case No. 523 of 1979. 

23. In light of the above discussions, we are of the view that the case property is not a vested property, rather it has been included in the list of vested property by violating the provision of the law. Therefore, the inclusion of the property in the schedule 'Ka' of the vested property list, published in the Gazette notification dated 2-5¬2012, (Annexure-H) is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

24. In the above facts and circumstances of the case, we find merit in the Rule. 

25. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. 

26. The respondents are hereby directed to exclude the case property from `Ka' schedule of the vested property list published in Bangla-desh Gazette dated 2-5-2012 through a fresh Gazette notification within 60 (sixty) days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order positively.

Communicate the copy of this judgment and order to the concerned respondents at once.

End.
